related_questions.question: What are the consequences of hypertension?

text_blocks.snippet: Hypertension, or high blood pressure, can lead to a range of serious health consequences if left untreated. These include heart attack, stroke, kidney disease, vision loss, and sexual dysfunction. It can also contribute to heart failure, aneurysms, and even cognitive decline, including dementia.
snippet_highlighted_words: heart attack, stroke, kidney disease, vision loss, and sexual dysfunction

list.title: Heart Attack:
list.snippet: Hypertension can damage arteries, leading to plaque buildup and blockages that restrict blood flow to the heart muscle, causing a heart attack.

list.title: Stroke:
list.snippet: High blood pressure can cause blood vessels in the brain to rupture or become blocked, leading to a stroke.

list.title: Heart Failure:
list.snippet: The heart has to work harder to pump blood against high pressure, which can lead to its enlargement and eventual failure to pump effectively.

list.title: Coronary Artery Disease:
list.snippet: High blood pressure is a major risk factor for coronary artery disease, where arteries supplying blood to the heart become narrowed or blocked.

list.title: Peripheral Artery Disease:
list.snippet: Hypertension can also affect arteries in the legs and feet, causing reduced blood flow and potentially leading to pain, infections, or even amputations.

list.title: Kidney Disease:
list.snippet: Damaged arteries in the kidneys can impair their ability to filter blood, leading to kidney disease and potentially kidney failure.

list.title: Vision Loss:
list.snippet: Hypertension can damage blood vessels in the eyes, potentially leading to vision problems or even blindness.

list.title: Sexual Dysfunction:
list.snippet: High blood pressure can contribute to erectile dysfunction in men and lower sex drive in women.

list.title: Cognitive Decline:
list.snippet: Hypertension has been linked to memory loss, impaired thinking, and an increased risk of dementia.

list.title: Aneurysm:
list.snippet: High blood pressure can weaken blood vessel walls, potentially leading to the formation of aneurysms, which are balloon-like bulges that can rupture.

list.title: Metabolic Syndrome:
list.snippet: Hypertension is a component of metabolic syndrome, which increases the risk of developing heart disease, stroke, and type 2 diabetes.

text_blocks.snippet: Hypertension, also known as high blood pressure, significantly increases the risk of several serious health conditions. These include heart disease, stroke, heart failure, kidney disease, and eye problems. Hypertension can also contribute to other issues like aneurysms, peripheral artery disease, and even vascular dementia.
snippet_highlighted_words: heart disease, stroke, heart failure, kidney disease, and eye problems

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the risks:

list.title: Heart Disease and Heart Attack:
list.snippet: Hypertension damages blood vessels, making them less elastic and more prone to plaque buildup. This can lead to coronary artery disease, and if a blood vessel to the heart becomes blocked, a heart attack can occur.

list.title: Stroke:
list.snippet: High blood pressure can cause blood vessels in the brain to weaken and rupture (hemorrhagic stroke) or become blocked (ischemic stroke), leading to brain damage.

list.title: Heart Failure:
list.snippet: The heart has to work harder to pump blood against increased pressure in the arteries, which can lead to heart failure over time.

list.title: Kidney Disease:
list.snippet: Hypertension can damage the blood vessels in the kidneys, impairing their ability to filter waste and potentially leading to kidney failure.

list.title: Eye Problems:
list.snippet: High blood pressure can damage blood vessels in the retina, leading to vision problems, and in severe cases, vision loss.

list.title: Aneurysms:
list.snippet: The constant pressure can weaken artery walls, causing them to bulge (aneurysms), which can be life-threatening if they rupture, according to the Mayo Clinic.

list.title: Dementia:
list.snippet: Hypertension can contribute to vascular dementia, a type of dementia caused by reduced blood flow to the brain.

list.title: Peripheral Artery Disease:
list.snippet: Hypertension can damage blood vessels in the legs and feet, leading to peripheral artery disease, which can cause pain, numbness, and in severe cases, amputation.

list.title: Complications during pregnancy:
list.snippet: High blood pressure during pregnancy can increase the risk of complications for both the mother and the baby.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: Many people with hypertension don't experience any noticeable symptoms, which is why it's often called the "silent killer". Regular blood pressure checks are crucial for early detection and management.
